examples.question_text:
A zoo has a baby animal born on $30\%$ of days. It publishes an article on $90\%$ of days with a birth and on $20\%$ of days without a birth.

Let $B$ mean a birth occurs and $A$ mean an article is published.

(a) Draw a probability tree.
(b) Given that an article was published, find the probability that a birth occurred.
(c) Given that an article was published, find the probability that no birth occurred.

A factory produces items of which $20\%$ are defective. Defective items fail an inspection $80\%$ of the time, while non-defective items pass $90\%$ of the time.

Let $D$ mean defective and $F$ mean fails inspection.

(a) Draw a probability tree.
(b) Given that an item failed inspection, find the probability that it is defective.
(c) Given that an item passed inspection, find the probability that it is non-defective.

Three six-sided dice have the following faces:

- Die 1: $1,2,3,4,5,6$.
- Die 2: $1,2,3,4,6,6$.
- Die 3: $1,2,3,6,6,6$.

Each face of each die is equally likely. One die is selected at random and rolled. Let $J_i$ mean Die $i$ is selected and $S$ mean a $6$ is rolled.

(a) Draw a probability tree.
(b) Given that a $6$ was rolled, find the probability that Die 1 was selected.
(c) Given that a $6$ was rolled, find the probability that Die 2 or Die 3 was selected.

methods.description: Multiply along the two paths leading to the observed outcome, add them for the denominator, and divide the required joint probability by that total. Either first-stage category may be requested.

methods.description: Find missing forward branch probabilities using complements, then calculate reverse conditional probability for the requested observed outcome, including a negative or passing result.

methods.description: Extend the tree to three first-stage categories. Sum every path producing the condition in the denominator; sum the relevant disjoint paths when the requested category is a union.

examples.derivation: Independently derived joint probabilities 0.27, 0.03, 0.14 and 0.56, summing to 1. Article probability is 0.41; the requested conditional probabilities are 27/41 and 14/41. Tree branches agree with the givens and complements. Matches the supplied zoo example's method.

Independently derived complementary branch probabilities 0.2 and 0.1 and joint probabilities 0.16, 0.04, 0.08 and 0.72, summing to 1. Failure probability is 0.24, giving 2/3 defective given failure. Passing probability is 0.76, giving 18/19 non-defective given passing. Tree labels and working agree.

Independent face counts give six probabilities 1/6, 2/6 and 3/6. With equal die-selection probabilities, the six joint paths are 1/18, 5/18, 2/18, 4/18, 3/18 and 3/18, summing to 1. P(S)=6/18; the requested probabilities are 1/6 and 5/6. The three-category tree and disjoint-path addition follow the supplied dice example and path-addition teaching.
